references.text: Daniel prophesies about rumors that will terrify the king: 'But rumors from the east and from the north shall terrify him' (Dan 11:44). The theme of wars and unrest signaling the end times has its roots in Daniel's prophecies.

Jeremiah describes war and destruction that is coming: 'War is proclaimed!' (Jer 4:19-22). The prophecy about wars and destruction as part of God's judgment forms the background for Jesus' words about wars and disturbances.

The parallel passage in Matthew: 'You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See to it that you are not alarmed! For this must take place, but the end is not yet' (Matt 24:6). This is the direct parallel to Luke 21:9 in Jesus' end-times discourse.

The parallel passage in Mark: 'When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed! This must take place, but the end is not yet' (Mark 13:7). Mark's version of the same end-times discourse on the Mount of Olives.

In Chronicles, a time of great unrest is described: 'In those days there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in. For great unrest was among all the inhabitants of the lands' (2 Chron 15:5-6). Disturbances and lack of peace among people are themes reflected in Jesus' words about ἀκαταστασίας (disturbances).

Revelation depicts wars as part of end-time events through the red horse: 'It was granted to him who sat on it to take peace from the earth, so that people would slay one another' (Rev 6:1-4). Wars belong to the events that must happen, but which do not yet mean the end has come.

Paul urges the Thessalonians not to be 'shaken in mind or alarmed' by claims that the day of the Lord has come (2 Thess 2:2). This reflects Jesus' exhortation not to be alarmed (μὴ πτοηθῆτε) and that the end will not come immediately.

Isaiah urges the people not to fear what others fear, but to regard the Lord as holy (Isa 8:12-13). The exhortation not to be frightened by external threats has parallels with Jesus' words about not being afraid when wars and disturbances occur.

Daniel reveals that God makes known 'what shall happen in the last days' (Dan 2:28-29). The expression δεῖ ταῦτα γενέσθαι (this must take place) in Luke 21:9 reflects the divine necessity in Daniel's prophecies about what must come.
